A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGD convergence-time research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, references, and appendices. The original auxiliary-results Appendix F is retained as Appendix G in v2.

before.justification: Figure 2 reports original simulations on the modified three-hump camel function, with 500 SGD runs per learning rate, empirical hitting-time distributions, and fitted convergence trends.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and adds original hitting-time experiments on the Styblinski–Tang and Himmelblau functions in Appendix F and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze the same constant-step-size SGD procedure and stochastic gradient oracle. The added examples and proof explanations introduce no algorithmic component or modification.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds two-dimensional Styblinski–Tang and Himmelblau evaluations to the retained three-hump camel example. This modestly broadens synthetic landscape coverage, including a landscape without spurious minima.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing optimization algorithms. The numerical comparisons remain between theoretical predictions and fitted SGD runtime data; newly cited methods are not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 2 retains the stated Gaussian noise, initialization near p3, and stopping tolerance, but its learning-rate tick values occur at different horizontal positions in v2. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects a revised learning-rate sweep or a plotting change. Appendix F otherwise reuses the existing evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a diagnostic comparison of exponential learning-rate dependence on Styblinski–Tang with the predicted subexponential regime on Himmelblau. This empirically examines the consequence of having no spurious minima, whereas v1's numerical analysis covers the positive-barrier camel example.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 runs per learning rate, empirical runtime distributions, and regression goodness-of-fit. The added experiments follow this practice; there is no reported increase in repetitions or new confidence intervals, seed disclosure, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Appendix F adds runtime distributions and reported theory/data fit R-squared pairs of 0.973/0.989 for Styblinski–Tang and 0.913/0.976 for Himmelblau, alongside the exponential versus subexponential finding. Figure 2 retains its reported data/theory values of 0.99/0.97. These are additional results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The main theorems, assumptions, and substantive bounds are retained. v2 removes v1's separate unrestricted pointwise transition-cost definition, Definition 5 and equation B.28, and changes the references in Lemma C.5 to the definition of costs that avoid other critical components. This is limited formal cleanup; the new proof overview does not establish a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal sharp-convergence claims remain stable. The conclusion adds the stronger assertion that escaping exponential complexity requires logarithmic scaling of spurious-minimum depth with problem dimension, and connects this to neural-network width or depth.

C2.justification: v2 explains polynomial depth dependence under objective-dependent noise and elaborates why local escape times do not determine global convergence time. Appendix B.1 explains the attracting-strength condition's role. Conversely, Figure 2 drops the interpretation linking two distribution modes to direct and indirect transition paths.

D1.justification: Appendix F supplies formulas, dimensionality, Gaussian noise level, stopping tolerance, and fixed-initialization information for the new numerical examples. These are additional experimental specifications; no code release or substantial implementation documentation is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on saddle avoidance, stochastic approximation, and Langevin or diffusion methods, and expands Appendix A's discussion of diffusion approximations and local escape times. The central positioning around global hitting times for discrete-time SGD remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives wording corrections and explanatory additions. A new Appendix B.1 provides a proof roadmap, and numerical validation becomes Appendix F, shifting auxiliary results to G. The overall argument and most appendix prose retain their structure.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises the visual presentation: it adds the proof-dependency diagram in Figure 3 and the multipanel experimental Figure 4, replaces Figure 1's illustrated SGD trajectory, and redraws Figure 2 using boxes and individual points instead of colored density overlays. Figure placement and axis labeling also change.

improvement.justification: The proof roadmap makes the lengthy argument easier to follow, while Appendix F extends the original illustration to both exponential and subexponential regimes. These provide modest gains with the principal theory unchanged. Benefits are tempered by unexplained Figure 2 axis changes, outdated section labels in Figure 3, and the new dimensional-scaling claim lacking a corresponding derivation.
